key_insight: CORNETO does not infer biological networks equally reliably in every setting. Its robustness depends on how much data and prior biological knowledge are available, as well as regularization and biological context.
problem_solved: Determining when CORNETO, an existing multi-omics network inference framework, can be reliably reused across datasets and biological settings.
method: Evaluate the reusability of CORNETO for learning biological networks from multi-omics data.
Examine how data availability, prior knowledge and regularization influence inference robustness.
Identify distinct robustness regimes across biological contexts.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the findings highlight that reliable reuse requires checking data coverage, prior knowledge and regularization rather than assuming a framework transfers unchanged. This can guide model configuration and interpretation of inferred biological networks.
visual_elements: Workflow: multi-omics data and prior biological knowledge → CORNETO → inferred network.
Conceptual regime map with axes for data availability and prior knowledge, highlighting differing robustness regions.
Regularization dial illustrating its role in shaping network inference.
Side-by-side biological network diagrams illustrating stable versus variable inferred connections.
paper_title: Reusability report: multi-sample omics network inference operates in distinct robustness regimes defined by prior knowledge and data availability
paper_authors: Xabier Martínez-de-Morentin, Sumeer A. Khan, Itziar Cenzano, Robert Lehmann, Alberto Maillo
